startup_tech: Co-reactive has developed a continuous tubular CO2 mineralization reactor that allows for the well-known CO2 mineralization reaction to happen under economic conditions in industrial settings. [cite: 132] CO, is injected at multiple points along the reactors and monitored by sensors, enabling controlled mineral carbonation reactions under pressure. [cite: 133] The slurry is filtered to recover carbonated product, while fine particles are recycled for reuse; [cite: 134] the output serves as cement, concrete, or filler material. [cite: 135]

startup_howwork: The PFASigator is a compact, modular on-site PFAS destruction system used by municipal utilities, industrial facilities, and remediation contractors to permanently eliminate PFAS from contaminated water. [cite: 268] Customers integrate the system into existing treatment infrastructures or deploy it in a trailer for temporary service. [cite: 270] The fully automated process is operated via an integrated control panel or a remote device. [cite: 271] Real-time fluoride production is monitored as a direct measure of PFAS destruction. [cite: 272] The customer experience at temporary deployments concludes once the water is fully treated. [cite: 273] Continued performance is ensured at permanent installations, with routine monthly maintenance and reagent refills. [cite: 274] Most sites with PFAS contamination require complex water treatment systems. [cite: 275] The channel to market at these sites is wastewater treatment system engineers who can integrate PFASigator as one component of a full system for the end user. [cite: 276] A few industrial and emergency service applications allow direct sales/lease from Enspired to the end user. [cite: 277] The PFASigator is sold or leased with follow-on sales of reagent refills and maintenance contracts. [cite: 278]
startup_valueprop: Enspired's ideal customers include: government agencies, industrial facilities, and remediation contractors challenged by PFAS contamination and its associated liabilities. [cite: 280] Enspired delivers the PFASigator, a fully automated, on-site system that permanently deconstructs PFAS with no toxic byproducts, at up to 10x lower cost than landfill/incineration and ~50% cheaper than other viable destruction methods, eliminating transport and long-term liability. [cite: 281]
startup_competitors: The competitors include: Technology competitors: Supercritical Water Oxidation (SCWO), Electrochemical Oxidation (EO), and Hydrothermal Alkaline Treatment (HALT) require extreme operating conditions and generate hazardous byproducts. [cite: 282, 284] The traditional use case competitors, incineration and landfill disposal, are reaching capacity, incur high transportation costs, and have long-term liabilities. [cite: 285] The PFASigator sets itself apart by enabling permanent, true on-site and automated destruction with no toxic byproducts, a small footprint, and enhanced safety. [cite: 286]
startup_tech: PFAS-contaminated water enters their system, where a special blend of two safe treatment chemicals and UV light work together to break the PFAS apart at the molecular level: [cite: 293] Generation of Reactive Species: UV light activates electron donors to produce hydrated electrons, highly reactive species capable of attacking PFAS. [cite: 295] Some systems (e.g., nano-reactors) enhance this step by extending electron lifetime and improving efficiency. [cite: 296] Reductive PFAS Degradation: Hydrated electrons break the strong carbon-fluorine bonds in PFAS, converting them into fluoride ions and shorter, less harmful carbon fragments. [cite: 297] This is the core degradation step. [cite: 298] Oxidation and Byproduct Cleanup: Any remaining organics or treatment residues are oxidized using photoactivated processes, transforming them into non- toxic end products like CO, and water. [cite: 299] This ensures complete remediation with minimal secondary pollution. [cite: 300]
startup_techadv: Enspired's key technical advantage lies in its ability to break down the forever PFAS chemicals with no toxic byproducts or air emissions. [cite: 302]

startup_howwork: Aerleum offers a technology to capture $CO_{2}$ from ambient air or flue gases and convert it into purified e-methanol using green hydrogen. [cite: 456] It involves three main stages: [cite: 457] Capture: $CO_{2}$ from ambient air or flue gas streams is introduced into the system. [cite: 459] Convert: Green hydrogen is injected and the system is heated simultaneously to transform $CO_{2}$ and $H_{2}$ to crude methanol. [cite: 460] Purification & Supply: Methanol is purified according to end application and supplied directly to customers for use as a drop-in fuel or chemical feedstock within existing customer operations. [cite: 461]
startup_valueprop: Aerleum's target customers include: Maritime fuel suppliers like Maersk, CMA CGM, seeking cost-competitive green methanol to meet IMO decarbonization mandates. [cite: 470, 472] Aviation fuel producers and airlines like Lufthansa and Air France-KLM, looking for scalable synthetic fuels (SAF) due to requirements like EU ReFuelEU. [cite: 473] Chemical manufacturers like BASE, Dow, and Ineos require renewable methanol as a building block for plastics, resins, and other chemical intermediates. [cite: 476] Heavy industrial emitters like cement and steel plants need on-site $CO_{2}$ utilization to cut Scope 1 emissions and valorize captured $CO_{2}$. [cite: 477] Aerleum's proprietary bi-functional material integrates capture and conversion in a single reactor, cutting energy use by up to $4x,$ lowering CAPEX and OPEX, and enabling seamless on-site e-methanol production. [cite: 478] They deliver e-methanol at fossil cost parity and up to 90% $CO_{2}$ reduction, ready to drop into existing supply chains for effortless decarbonization. [cite: 479]
startup_competitors: The competitors include: Direct technology competitors like Carbon Recycling International (Iceland), which relies on separate $CO_{2}$ capture and conversion steps, leading to higher infrastructure and energy costs, and Twelve (USA), which operates through non-integrated processes with higher energy intensity. [cite: 481, 482] Indirect use-case competitors like Turn2X (Germany), Energo (France), which depend on external feedstock sourcing, and non-integrated processes, as well as many industrial players who rely on a fragmented and costly approach to conventional carbon capture and fuel production [cite: 484] Unlike these approaches, Aerleum combines capture and conversion in a single reactor using its proprietary bi-functional material, cutting energy demand by up to 4x, reducing costs through simpler operations, and enabling on-site, drop-in e-methanol production for seamless customer adoption. [cite: 485] In addition, Aerleum ensures independent, affordable, and scalable access to renewable $CO_{2}$ [cite: 486]
startup_tech: Aerleum has developed a single reactor that can both capture CO, and transform it into e-methanol using green hydrogen in one step, instead of relying on multiple complex systems. [cite: 493] CO₂ Capture: A bifunctional material (made of a sorbent plus a catalyst) is exposed to an air or flue gas stream so the sorbent physically adsorbs and captures the $CO_{2}.$ [cite: 494] Conversion: The CO₂ loaded bifunctional material is then contacted with a hydrogen flow, where the catalyst (positioned on the sorbent surface) converts the CO, into products such as methanol. [cite: 496] Integrated Functionality: The same material acts both as a sorbent and a catalyst (no extra support needed), combining capture and conversion into one process step. [cite: 497]
startup_techadv: Aerleum's unchanging core is its integrated reactor design, powered by a proprietary bi-functional material that captures and converts $CO_{2}$ in one step, delivering unmatched energy efficiency and cost savings. [cite: 499]
startup_ip: The venture has filed patents, including WO2025104406A1: Bifunctional material and use thereof in a method for capturing and converting carbon dioxide. [cite: 504] Additional filings are in progress. [cite: 505]

[cite: 640] The customer applies Bio.R or Bio.C as a liquid seed coating or in-furrow at planting, together with other standard inputs. [cite: 643] The bio-trained microbes colonize the root zone, boosting early growth and stress tolerance in saline, dry, or nutrient-poor soils. [cite: 644] Stronger roots and resilient plants lead to higher yields and improved crop performance at harvest. [cite: 645]
startup_valueprop: M4Life approaches its customers in two phases: Phase 1: medium-to large-scale farmers in stress-affected regions (B2C), with whom M4Life will validate its solutions, build a client portfolio, and gain market insights. [cite: 651, 653] Phase 2: distributors and input companies for B2B partnerships, allowing them to scale their impact through proven results and established customer demand. [cite: 654] M4Life products reduce agricultural risks and regenerate soils, delivering 10-25% yield gains and 40x ROI by mitigating crop stress. [cite: 655]
startup_competitors: The competitors include: Large multinationals such as BASF (Germany), Corteva (USA), Bayer (Germany), and Syngenta (Switzerland); [cite: 656, 659] Specialized biological companies including Novonesis (Denmark), ProFarm (USA) and Agrauxine (France). [cite: 659] Local and regional providers in Latin America who supply low-cost inoculants based on generic strains. [cite: 660] Most of these competitors rely on native or generalist microbes, which often underperform in fields affected by salinity, drought, or nutrient stress. [cite: 661] In contrast, M4Life's produces elite strains specifically adapted to these adverse conditions, thus offering an alternative to conventional inoculants. [cite: 662]
startup_tech: M4Life's technology mimics natural selection, but at an accelerated pace. [cite: 669] They expose beneficial microbes to harsh conditions and guide their evolution to enhance traits like stress resistance and plant growth promotion. [cite: 670] This process, called bio-training, results in "elite" microbial strains that are far more effective in real-world farming conditions than their native counterparts. [cite: 671] These strains are then formulated into liquid products that farmers apply to seeds, soil, or plants, helping crops thrive in degraded or salty soils. [cite: 672]
startup_techadv: The enhanced abiotic stress tolerance of M4Life's bio-trained microbial strains, which enables significant improvements in crop yield and resilience under challenging soil conditions, is the key dimension driving their value proposition. [cite: 674]
startup_ip: M4Life has filed a PCT patent: WO2025184140A1 (International, pending), modified and isolated strains of pseudomonas stutzeri rdc-01 and bacillus velezensis ca1, compositions used as inoculum for improving plant growth and abiotic stress resistance, methods and uses thereof. [cite: 679] The venture has pending IP protection with patent filings in the USA (via a PCT application) and Argentina, covering the bio-training process and the formulation of evolved microbial strains. [cite: 680]

[cite: 749, 799] It is tackling the climate-critical challenge of lime and cement emissions, which are chemically unavoidable with legacy methods and account for 8% of global CO2. [cite: 750, 800] CURA's breakthrough lies in CURALYTE(TM), a proprietary molecule that reduces energy use and cost by up to 50% compared to conventional cement manufacture with CCS. [cite: 751, 801]

startup_longtermview: By 2035, CURA will be the global standard for cement production. [cite: 803] Their CURALYTE(TM)-enabled electrolysis system will be deployed across hundreds of industrial sites worldwide, enabling decarbonization of over 20M tons of CO₂ annually, Ultimately, they aim to eliminate 3 Gt/yr of CO, emissions and contribute substantially to a net-zero industrial future. [cite: 804]
startup_howwork: CURA retrofits into existing cement facilities without requiring feedstock changes or new plant construction. [cite: 809] Customers begin with a site assessment and technoeconomic evaluation. [cite: 810] Once approved, CURA leads the engineering, build, and integration process, typically completed within 12-18 months. [cite: 811] The system produces a decarbonized lime feed for the clinker kiln and pure CO, ready for capture, utilization, or sale. [cite: 812]
startup_valueprop: CURA's ideal customers include cement producers who are actively seeking cost-effective pathways to decarbonize and meet ESG targets. [cite: 818] CURA provides modules that retrofit onto existing plants without disrupting feedstocks or supply chains while delivering up to 85% emissions reductions. [cite: 819] Unlike conventional CCS or greenfield solutions, CURA'S CURALYTE(TM)-powered technology enables up to 50% lower energy use and cost and is built on familiar processes, accelerating measurable progress toward net-zero with minimal operational risk. [cite: 820]
startup_competitors: The competitors include: Carbon Capture Retrofits: LEILAC (UK), Svante (Canada), Carbon Clean (UK) capture CO, after calcination, requiring large infrastructure and high energy; [cite: 822, 826] Alternative Feedstocks: Brimstone (USA) and Sublime Systems (USA) rely on calcium silicates, demanding new mines and supply chains; [cite: 827] Alternative Products (Non-OPC): LC3 (Switzerland), Cemfree (UK), and Sublime Systems develop non-OPC cements with limited structural adoption and long validation timelines; [cite: 828] Supplementary Cementitious Materials (SCMs): Terra CO₂ (USA), Eco Material (USA), and Carbon Limit (USA) reduce emissions in concrete blends but don't decarbonize cement production itself. [cite: 829] CURA captures 100% of process emissions at the source while producing standard OPC using existing materials, infrastructure, and workflows, delivering low- carbon cement without changing the product or the system. [cite: 830]
startup_tech: CURA uses a proprietary electrochemical process powered by CURALYTE(TM) to capture carbon emissions from cement production before they are released: Electricity powers the CURA module to create acidic and alkaline solutions. [cite: 837] The acid dissolves limestone, producing a calcium-rich solution and a pure stream of CO2 that can be directly compressed for utilization or storage. [cite: 839] This solution is then mixed with the alkaline solution to form hydrated lime [Ca(OH) ], which is filtered out, while the remaining solution is reused to generate more acid and alkalinity. [cite: 840]
startup_techadv: The key advantage of CURA's technology is CURALYTE(TM), a proprietary molecule that enables ultra-low voltage electrolysis, dramatically reducing the energy and cost of operation. [cite: 842]
startup_ip: CURA has filed multiple patents, including: A patent family of US18/730,401, CA3248839, CN202380028215.1, EP23742649.9 for "Methods and apparatus for converting metal carbonate salts to metal hydroxides"; [cite: 846, 847] PCT/CA2025/050128: "Methods and systems for converting metal ion-containing solids to useful products", which cover CURA's novel pre-calcination. [cite: 848] The founders have an exclusive license for all the IP listed by the University of British Columbia. [cite: 849]

[cite: 933, 983] Existing ESD packaging is costly and petroleum-based, but Intace has invented a biopolymer that provides reliable ESD protection while also being biodegradable, low- cost, and reducing waste management fees by up to 30%, since no additives are required. [cite: 934, 984]

startup_longtermview: Intace aims to become the primary manufacturer of biodegradable conductive foam for electronic packaging, capturing 5% of the $1.7B global market by selling 2,500 tons annually, and reducing over 6,000 tons of CO2 emissions per year. [cite: 986]
startup_howwork: An electronics company seeking to decarbonize its supply chain without compromising anti-static performance will buy Intace's bio-foarn sheets as its packaging solution. [cite: 991] Depending on customer needs, the bio-foam sheets will be cut and shaped to pack their products properly. [cite: 992] For a packaging manufacturer, Intace's drop-in solution would be licensed so they can produce the bio-foam locally. [cite: 993] Incorporating Intace's proprietary conductive formulation into a customer's biodegradable polymer matrix produces a foam with reliable electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection, eliminating the need for toxic additives or surface treatments. [cite: 994]
startup_valueprop: Intace's ideal customers are electronics and semiconductor manufacturers, as well as packaging suppliers serving these sectors. [cite: 997] These companies ship high- value, sensitive components such as circuit boards, integrated chips, and consumer electronics that require ESD-safe and shock-absorbing packaging. [cite: 998] These customers face growing pressure to reduce plastic waste, meet aggressive sustainability targets, and minimize product loss due to static discharge or impact damage, all while maintaining competitive costs. [cite: 999] Currently, there are no bio-based foams on the market that meet the mechanical and ESD performance standards required by these industries. [cite: 1000] Intace offers a seaweed-based conductive foam that is fully compliant with antistatic and packaging safety requirements. [cite: 1001] The material eliminates dusting, supports cleanroom compatibility, and can be integrated into existing packaging systems without process changes. [cite: 1002] It delivers this performance at a price parity with petroleum-based foams, at a £2.2K GBP/m3 retail price. [cite: 1003]
startup_competitors: Intace's primary competitors are legacy packaging companies that produce petroleum-based ESD foams. [cite: 1005] (UFP, ATLAS, Wisconsin Foam) These materials are low-cost and high-performance but are neither recyclable nor compostable, contributing significantly to plastic pollution. [cite: 1006] In contrast, Intace's seaweed-based conductive foam is home-compostable, microplastic-free, and does not require industrial recycling, all while maintaining price parity with traditional foams. [cite: 1007] Emerging sustainable packaging companies such as Mushroom Packaging, Cruz Foam, and Ecovative offer bio-based solutions, but their products generally lack ESD protection, fall short in technical performance, and often carry a 2-5x green premium. [cite: 1008] Intace's foam stands apart by delivering superior surface resistivity in the antistatic range (109-1011 ohms/sq), reduced fragility, and dust-free performance, meeting the strict technical requirements of the electronics industry without compromising on sustainability or cost. [cite: 1009]
startup_tech: Intace has developed a molecular engineering platform that programs natural, plant-based polymers to perform like advanced plastics during use and then safely deconstruct at the end of their life. [cite: 1016] The process realigns molecular chains and binds them in controlled patterns, enabling the creation of materials with tailored strength and durability under pressure, heat, or impact. [cite: 1017] The materials can be triggered to break down harmlessly without leaving microplastics behind and enabling high-performance, sustainable packaging without the need for added chemicals or synthetic coatings. [cite: 1018]
startup_techadv: Intace technology is built on a novel polymer crosslinking and destabilization process for molecular manipulation that shapes the molecular structure and lifecycle of natural polymer. [cite: 1021] This allows the creation of a rare and unique combination for packaging with conductive foams that are both antistatic and biodegradable (compostable at home). [cite: 1022]
startup_ip: Intace filed their patent on October 2025 through the UK Green Channel. [cite: 1027] The patent considers both the product and the underlying process technology. [cite: 1028] This includes the proprietary method of polymer crosslinking and destabilization that enables programmable molecular manipulation of natural materials, resulting in conductivity without the use of additives. [cite: 1029]

[cite: 1099, 1147] The company addresses the critical challenge of renewable intermittency by providing safe, affordable, and scalable storage to balance supply and demand, reduce energy waste, and enable 24/7 clean power for grids, industry, critical infrastructure and others. [cite: 1100, 1148] What distinguishes HalioGen is its no-membrane architecture that simplifies design, cuts costs by ~20%, avoids scarce materials like lithium and vanadium, and delivers durable, recyclable, and fire-safe systems capable of operating in extreme climates. [cite: 1101, 1149]

startup_longtermview: Over the next decade, HalioGen Power targets a significant energy cost reduction for their batteries below $50/kWh and round-trip efficiencies above 85%. [cite: 1151] HalioGen intends to position itself as the backbone of the medium-duration storage segment (8-16 hours), and the team aspires, through mass manufacturing, to capture about 3% of the total market, yielding a $2B USD market by 2050. [cite: 1152]
startup_howwork: Clients receive a modular, plug-and-play energy storage system that integrates seamlessly with renewable generation, grids, or microgrids. [cite: 1156] It stores energy when supply is high and releases it during peak demand, enabling efficient use of renewable energy. [cite: 1157] Haliogen Power operates a B2B model, providing battery units customized to clients' specific energy storage capacity needs. [cite: 1158]
startup_valueprop: Ideal customers are utilities, large commercial & industrial users (e.g., data centres, manufacturing, mining), and operators of critical infrastructure such as ports, hospitals, and airports. [cite: 1161] These organisations require reliable 24/7 clean energy, face high curtailment or grid congestion costs, and need long-duration storage to stabilise operations while decarbonising. [cite: 1162] The customers would benefit from a strengthened grid with a regulated continuous energy supply, lower electricity costs under £40/kWh at scale, and a lower energy loss during the charge and discharge process due to a high Round-Trip Efficiency (RTE) of ~90%. [cite: 1163] HalioGen Power provides up to 70% lower CAPEX than conventional flow batteries, with a 20+ year lifespan. [cite: 1164] These non-flammable batteries work on water- based electrolytes and have stable performance across -10°C to +55°C, eliminating fire and cooling risks. [cite: 1165]
startup_competitors: Invinity and CellCube (and others) are working on vanadium-based flow batteries, but this technology is expensive (£250+/kWh installed) and delivers low RTE (less than 80%). [cite: 1167] ESS, ESI, Voltstorage are developing Iron and organic storage-based systems, but they suffer from lower efficiencies due to electrolyte degradation. [cite: 1168] Lithium batteries degrade over time with a life expectancy of 8 years and are, by nature, short-duration energy storage, economical for up to 6 hours of duration. [cite: 1169] Lithium batteries are also flammable and therefore not safe for a number of applications. [cite: 1170] Haliogen Power's no-membrane flow batteries offer resilience, better affordability and safety, at a higher efficiency of 85% RTE. [cite: 1171]
startup_tech: HalioGen Power is developing a non-flammable and no-membrane flow battery designed for a 10 to 16-hour duration. [cite: 1178] The battery electrolytes (zinc and bromine in aqueous solution) are stored in one tank, where they naturally separate by density (like when "mixing oil and water"). [cite: 1180] During charging and discharging, the electrolytes are pumped through an electrochemical stack, which is designed to be mass-manufactured at a very low cost using abundant, recyclable materials and water-based electrolytes. startup_valueprop: PhaseTree helps customers in the steels, batteries, and advanced alloy industries by amplifying their materials discovery processes. [cite: 1340] The platform delivers step-change acceleration, by delivering results in 2-3 months that otherwise would have taken several years. [cite: 1341] This rapid development drives substantial customer savings on both OPEX and CAPEX; [cite: 1342] bringing new materials to market typically costs over $100M, an order of magnitude more than what is achievable using simulation-driven approaches. [cite: 1343] Unlike competitors, Phase Tree covers the end-to-end process from conceptualization all the way to synthesized material. [cite: 1344]
startup_competitors: Competitors mainly fall in one of two categories: Point solutions: Competitors which requires a combination of software and material science to stitch together: Exomatter (DEU), Dassault (FRA), Chemify (UK), SCM (NL), Quantistry (DEU) [cite: 1346, 1348] Indirect solutions: competitors who use foundational Al models to screen & generate huge libraries of novel candidates: Cusp.ai (UK), Orbital (UK), Radical AI (USA), Atomic Tesselator (NZL) [cite: 1349] Phase Tree integrates seamlessly into customers' existing discovery processes, guiding the selection of candidates for synthesis, all without requiring in-house material science or software expertise. [cite: 1350] By covering the entire journey from idea inception to synthesis, Phase Tree is distinctly differentiated from competitors across both categories. [cite: 1351]
startup_tech: Phase Tree's innovation stems from a physics-first approach augmented with Al. [cite: 1358] At the core sits a set of peer-verified quanturm-accurate calculations about materials systerns. [cite: 1359] Once compiled, these quantum-accurate calculations are fed to machine learning models that can scale these systems up to sizes that are otherwise intractable, even on modern compute infrastructure. [cite: 1360] Achieving this significantly enlarged view of atomic systems allows us to start generating predictions about properties, synthesisability, and real-world behavior beyond what is otherwise achievable. [cite: 1361]
startup_techadv: The critical technological aspect of the platform is the multiscale "glue" that allows Phase Tree to seamlessly bridge and productize otherwise uncoupled physical principles. [cite: 1363] This multiscale bridging not only retains critical property data across the different scales that would otherwise be lost when transferred with point solutions, but it also enables a bi-directional flow of data, such that information from synthesized materials downstream can be fed back into our Al models upstream to improve their precision and value. [cite: 1365] This recursive learning loop for Al forms the core of our long-term competitive advantage and will continue to be at the center of what we're building. [cite: 1366]

startup_howwork: Mykor is developing a portfolio of products for insulative building systems: MykoSIP Internal - Mykor's flagship product is a prefabricated structural insulated panel that replaces three separate products that are usually brought together onsite. [cite: 1507, 1508] It is a non load bearing solution for partition walls that requires 20% less structural framing than other insulation systems. [cite: 1509] Mykor's wall system replaces the traditional multi-layer construction process with a single, prefabricated bio-based panel that integrates structure, insulation, and facing into one unit. [cite: 1510] Each panel is manufactured off-site using Mykor's mycelium-enhanced composite technology, producing a lightweight, fire-resistant, high-performance component with dramatically lower embodied carbon. [cite: 1511] Contractors simply install the modular panels like a standard prefabricated element. [cite: 1512] Its bio materials are non toxic, giving a better experience for the installers and offer breathability and mould prevention to the end user. [cite: 1513] Mykobead - Replacing a polystyrene bead, the Mykobead is sprayed into cavity walls and can be used as a retrofit solution. [cite: 1514] MykoSIP External - This load bearing product is a thicker and denser version of the first product, it is still in development and scheduled for commercialisation in 2027. [cite: 1515]
startup_valueprop: Mykor's ideal customer is a sustainability-driven prefabrication or principal construction contractor looking to accelerate build times, reduce embodied carbon, and modernise their supply chain. [cite: 1517] These companies already understand that traditional wall systems are slow, labour-heavy, and environmentally outdated, and they're actively looking for next-generation materials that deliver both performance and predictable cost savings. [cite: 1518] Strategic Partner Contractors (Primary Ideal Customer): These are large contractors capable of multi-year offtake agreements and committed to embedding low-carbon materials into their long-term pipeline. [cite: 1519] They're big enough to benefit from, and participate in, localised co-manufacturing through a joint venture structure. [cite: 1520] Large Contractors Purchasing Through Standard B2B Channels (Secondary Ideal Customer): These are major firms aiming to integrate sustainable prefabricated wall systems without entering a JV. [cite: 1521] They benefit from the performance advantages and sustainability profile of Mykor products at scale, but deploy them through traditional procurement routes. [cite: 1522] These customers receive a faster, cleaner, and future-ready wall system that reduces onsite labor costs and delays, with a 60% less embodied carbon than standard construction, 100% biodegradable non-toxic, Fire-resistant (Euroclass B) product. [cite: 1523] With strong acoustic and thermal performance, Mykor gives contractors a meaningful sustainability edge in regulated and ESG-driven markets. [cite: 1524]

startup_tech: Mykor produces proprietary insulation materials made entirely from bio residues and mycelium, the root structure of fungi. [cite: 1537] The mycelium naturally binds the waste into strong, lightweight panels that are thermally efficient, fire-resistant, and carbon-negative. [cite: 1538] The Grow technology is the core tech that allows Mykor to control the mycelium, in order to be able to achieve a scalable, low energy and cost process, requiring no plastic. [cite: 1539] Through Mykor's controlled growth process, these materials are scaled into MykoSIP, a bio-based structural insulated panel (SIP) that replaces synthetic foams such as expanded polystyrene insulation (EPS) and extruded polystyrene insulation (XPS), combining the benefits of natural materials with the performance of modern building technologies. [cite: 1540]
startup_techadv: A proprietary low-energy, low-cost "Grow" process, which uses agricultural byproducts to cultivate mycelium-based insulation at industrial volumes which is something no other mycelium company has achieved to date.
